name: xcodebuildmcp

tools.name: build_device
tools.description: Builds an app from a project or workspace for a physical Apple device. Provide exactly one of projectPath or workspacePath. Example: build_device({ projectPath: '/path/to/MyProject.xcodeproj', scheme: 'MyScheme' })

extraArgs.description: Additional arguments to pass to xcodebuild

tools.name: clean
tools.description: Cleans build products for either a project or a workspace using xcodebuild. Provide exactly one of projectPath or workspacePath. Platform defaults to iOS if not specified. Example: clean({ projectPath: '/path/to/MyProject.xcodeproj', scheme: 'MyScheme', platform: 'iOS' })

configuration.description: Optional: Build configuration to clean (Debug, Release, etc.)

derivedDataPath.description: Optional: Path where derived data might be located

preferXcodebuild.description: If true, prefers xcodebuild over the experimental incremental build system, useful for when incremental build system fails.

platform.description: Optional: Platform to clean for (defaults to iOS). Choose from macOS, iOS, iOS Simulator, watchOS, watchOS Simulator, tvOS, tvOS Simulator, visionOS, visionOS Simulator

tools.name: discover_projs
tools.description: Scans a directory (defaults to workspace root) to find Xcode project (.xcodeproj) and workspace (.xcworkspace) files.

workspaceRoot.description: The absolute path of the workspace root to scan within.

scanPath.description: Optional: Path relative to workspace root to scan. Defaults to workspace root.

maxDepth.description: Optional: Maximum directory depth to scan. Defaults to 5.

tools.name: get_app_bundle_id
tools.description: Extracts the bundle identifier from an app bundle (.app) for any Apple platform (iOS, iPadOS, watchOS, tvOS, visionOS). IMPORTANT: You MUST provide the appPath parameter. Example: get_app_bundle_id({ appPath: '/path/to/your/app.app' })

appPath.description: Path to the .app bundle to extract bundle ID from (full path to the .app directory)

tools.name: get_device_app_path
tools.description: Gets the app bundle path for a physical device application (iOS, watchOS, tvOS, visionOS) using either a project or workspace. Provide exactly one of projectPath or workspacePath. Example: get_device_app_path({ projectPath: '/path/to/project.xcodeproj', scheme: 'MyScheme' })

tools.name: install_app_device
tools.description: Installs an app on a physical Apple device (iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch, Apple TV, Apple Vision Pro). Requires deviceId and appPath.

deviceId.description: UDID of the device (obtained from list_devices)

appPath.description: Path to the .app bundle to install (full path to the .app directory)

tools.name: launch_app_device
tools.description: Launches an app on a physical Apple device (iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch, Apple TV, Apple Vision Pro). Requires deviceId and bundleId.

deviceId.description: UDID of the device (obtained from list_devices)

bundleId.description: Bundle identifier of the app to launch (e.g., "com.example.MyApp")

tools.name: list_devices
tools.description: Lists connected physical Apple devices (iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch, Apple TV, Apple Vision Pro) with their UUIDs, names, and connection status. Use this to discover physical devices for testing.

tools.name: list_schemes
tools.description: Lists available schemes for either a project or a workspace. Provide exactly one of projectPath or workspacePath. Example: list_schemes({ projectPath: '/path/to/MyProject.xcodeproj' })

tools.name: show_build_settings
tools.description: Shows build settings from either a project or workspace using xcodebuild. Provide exactly one of projectPath or workspacePath, plus scheme. Example: show_build_settings({ projectPath: '/path/to/MyProject.xcodeproj', scheme: 'MyScheme' })

scheme.description: Scheme name to show build settings for (Required)

tools.name: start_device_log_cap
tools.description: Starts capturing logs from a specified Apple device (iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch, Apple TV, Apple Vision Pro) by launching the app with console output. Returns a session ID.

deviceId.description: UDID of the device (obtained from list_devices)

bundleId.description: Bundle identifier of the app to launch and capture logs for.

tools.name: stop_app_device
tools.description: Stops an app running on a physical Apple device (iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch, Apple TV, Apple Vision Pro). Requires deviceId and processId.

deviceId.description: UDID of the device (obtained from list_devices)

processId.description: Process ID (PID) of the app to stop

tools.name: stop_device_log_cap
tools.description: Stops an active Apple device log capture session and returns the captured logs.

logSessionId.description: The session ID returned by start_device_log_cap.

tools.name: test_device
tools.description: Runs tests for an Apple project or workspace on a physical device (iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch, Apple TV, Apple Vision Pro) using xcodebuild test and parses xcresult output. Provide exactly one of projectPath or workspacePath. IMPORTANT: Requires scheme and deviceId. Example: test_device({ projectPath: "/path/to/MyProject.xcodeproj", scheme: "MyScheme", deviceId: "device-uuid" })

deviceId.description: UDID of the device (obtained from list_devices)

extraArgs.description: Additional arguments to pass to xcodebuild

testRunnerEnv.description: Environment variables to pass to the test runner (TEST_RUNNER_ prefix added automatically)

tools.name: doctor
tools.description: Provides comprehensive information about the MCP server environment, available dependencies, and configuration status.

enabled.description: Optional: dummy parameter to satisfy MCP protocol

tools.name: start_sim_log_cap
tools.description: Starts capturing logs from a specified simulator. Returns a session ID. By default, captures only structured logs.

simulatorUuid.description: UUID of the simulator to capture logs from (obtained from list_simulators).

bundleId.description: Bundle identifier of the app to capture logs for.

captureConsole.description: Whether to capture console output (requires app relaunch).

tools.name: stop_sim_log_cap
tools.description: Stops an active simulator log capture session and returns the captured logs.

logSessionId.description: The session ID returned by start_sim_log_cap.

tools.name: build_macos
tools.description: Builds a macOS app using xcodebuild from a project or workspace. Provide exactly one of projectPath or workspacePath. Example: build_macos({ projectPath: '/path/to/MyProject.xcodeproj', scheme: 'MyScheme' })

derivedDataPath.description: Path where build products and other derived data will go

arch.description: Architecture to build for (arm64 or x86_64). For macOS only.

preferXcodebuild.description: If true, prefers xcodebuild over the experimental incremental build system

tools.name: build_run_macos
tools.description: Builds and runs a macOS app from a project or workspace in one step. Provide exactly one of projectPath or workspacePath. Example: build_run_macos({ projectPath: '/path/to/MyProject.xcodeproj', scheme: 'MyScheme' })

derivedDataPath.description: Path where build products and other derived data will go

arch.description: Architecture to build for (arm64 or x86_64). For macOS only.

preferXcodebuild.description: If true, prefers xcodebuild over the experimental incremental build system

tools.name: get_mac_app_path
tools.description: Gets the app bundle path for a macOS application using either a project or workspace. Provide exactly one of projectPath or workspacePath. Example: get_mac_app_path({ projectPath: '/path/to/project.xcodeproj', scheme: 'MyScheme' })

extraArgs.description: Additional arguments to pass to xcodebuild

arch.description: Architecture to build for (arm64 or x86_64). For macOS only.

tools.name: get_mac_bundle_id
tools.description: Extracts the bundle identifier from a macOS app bundle (.app). IMPORTANT: You MUST provide the appPath parameter. Example: get_mac_bundle_id({ appPath: '/path/to/your/app.app' }) Note: In some environments, this tool may be prefixed as mcp0_get_macos_bundle_id.

appPath.description: Path to the macOS .app bundle to extract bundle ID from (full path to the .app directory)

tools.name: launch_mac_app
tools.description: Launches a macOS application. IMPORTANT: You MUST provide the appPath parameter. Example: launch_mac_app({ appPath: '/path/to/your/app.app' }) Note: In some environments, this tool may be prefixed as mcp0_launch_macos_app.

appPath.description: Path to the macOS .app bundle to launch (full path to the .app directory)

args.description: Additional arguments to pass to the app

tools.name: stop_mac_app
tools.description: Stops a running macOS application. Can stop by app name or process ID.

appName.description: Name of the application to stop (e.g., "Calculator" or "MyApp")

processId.description: Process ID (PID) of the application to stop

tools.name: test_macos
tools.description: Runs tests for a macOS project or workspace using xcodebuild test and parses xcresult output. Provide exactly one of projectPath or workspacePath. IMPORTANT: Requires scheme. Example: test_macos({ projectPath: "/path/to/MyProject.xcodeproj", scheme: "MyScheme" })

derivedDataPath.description: Path where build products and other derived data will go

preferXcodebuild.description: If true, prefers xcodebuild over the experimental incremental build system

testRunnerEnv.description: Environment variables to pass to the test runner (TEST_RUNNER_ prefix added automatically)

tools.name: scaffold_ios_project
tools.description: Scaffold a new iOS project from templates. Creates a modern Xcode project with workspace structure, SPM package for features, and proper iOS configuration.

outputPath.description: Path where the project should be created

bundleIdentifier.description: Bundle identifier (e.g., com.example.myapp). If not provided, will use com.example.projectname

displayName.description: App display name (shown on home screen/dock). If not provided, will use projectName

marketingVersion.description: Marketing version (e.g., 1.0, 2.1.3). If not provided, will use 1.0

currentProjectVersion.description: Build number (e.g., 1, 42, 100). If not provided, will use 1

customizeNames.description: Whether to customize project names and identifiers. Default is true.

deploymentTarget.description: iOS deployment target (e.g., 18.4, 17.0). If not provided, will use 18.4

tools.name: scaffold_macos_project
tools.description: Scaffold a new macOS project from templates. Creates a modern Xcode project with workspace structure, SPM package for features, and proper macOS configuration.

outputPath.description: Path where the project should be created

bundleIdentifier.description: Bundle identifier (e.g., com.example.myapp). If not provided, will use com.example.projectname

displayName.description: App display name (shown on home screen/dock). If not provided, will use projectName

marketingVersion.description: Marketing version (e.g., 1.0, 2.1.3). If not provided, will use 1.0

currentProjectVersion.description: Build number (e.g., 1, 42, 100). If not provided, will use 1

customizeNames.description: Whether to customize project names and identifiers. Default is true.

deploymentTarget.description: macOS deployment target (e.g., 15.4, 14.0). If not provided, will use 15.4

tools.name: boot_sim
tools.description: Boots an iOS simulator. After booting, use open_sim() to make the simulator visible. IMPORTANT: You MUST provide the simulatorUuid parameter. Example: boot_sim({ simulatorUuid: 'YOUR_UUID_HERE' })

simulatorUuid.description: UUID of the simulator to use (obtained from list_simulators)

tools.name: build_run_sim
tools.description: Builds and runs an app from a project or workspace on a specific simulator by UUID or name. Provide exactly one of projectPath or workspacePath, and exactly one of simulatorId or simulatorName. IMPORTANT: Requires either projectPath or workspacePath, plus scheme and either simulatorId or simulatorName. Example: build_run_sim({ projectPath: '/path/to/MyProject.xcodeproj', scheme: 'MyScheme', simulatorName: 'iPhone 16' })

projectPath.description: Path to .xcodeproj file. Provide EITHER this OR workspacePath, not both

workspacePath.description: Path to .xcworkspace file. Provide EITHER this OR projectPath, not both

simulatorId.description: UUID of the simulator (from list_sims). Provide EITHER this OR simulatorName, not both

simulatorName.description: Name of the simulator (e.g., 'iPhone 16'). Provide EITHER this OR simulatorId, not both

derivedDataPath.description: Path where build products and other derived data will go

useLatestOS.description: Whether to use the latest OS version for the named simulator

preferXcodebuild.description: If true, prefers xcodebuild over the experimental incremental build system, useful for when incremental build system fails.

tools.name: build_sim
tools.description: Builds an app from a project or workspace for a specific simulator by UUID or name. Provide exactly one of projectPath or workspacePath, and exactly one of simulatorId or simulatorName. IMPORTANT: Requires either projectPath or workspacePath, plus scheme and either simulatorId or simulatorName. Example: build_sim({ projectPath: '/path/to/MyProject.xcodeproj', scheme: 'MyScheme', simulatorName: 'iPhone 16' })

projectPath.description: Path to .xcodeproj file. Provide EITHER this OR workspacePath, not both

workspacePath.description: Path to .xcworkspace file. Provide EITHER this OR projectPath, not both

simulatorId.description: UUID of the simulator (from list_sims). Provide EITHER this OR simulatorName, not both

simulatorName.description: Name of the simulator (e.g., 'iPhone 16'). Provide EITHER this OR simulatorId, not both

derivedDataPath.description: Path where build products and other derived data will go

useLatestOS.description: Whether to use the latest OS version for the named simulator

preferXcodebuild.description: If true, prefers xcodebuild over the experimental incremental build system, useful for when incremental build system fails.

tools.name: describe_ui
tools.description: Gets entire view hierarchy with precise frame coordinates (x, y, width, height) for all visible elements. Use this before UI interactions or after layout changes - do NOT guess coordinates from screenshots. Returns JSON tree with frame data for accurate automation.

tools.name: get_sim_app_path
tools.description: Gets the app bundle path for a simulator by UUID or name using either a project or workspace file. IMPORTANT: Requires either projectPath OR workspacePath (not both), plus scheme, platform, and either simulatorId OR simulatorName (not both). Example: get_sim_app_path({ projectPath: '/path/to/project.xcodeproj', scheme: 'MyScheme', platform: 'iOS Simulator', simulatorName: 'iPhone 16' })

projectPath.description: Path to .xcodeproj file. Provide EITHER this OR workspacePath, not both

workspacePath.description: Path to .xcworkspace file. Provide EITHER this OR projectPath, not both

simulatorId.description: UUID of the simulator (from list_sims). Provide EITHER this OR simulatorName, not both

simulatorName.description: Name of the simulator (e.g., 'iPhone 16'). Provide EITHER this OR simulatorId, not both

useLatestOS.description: Whether to use the latest OS version for the named simulator

tools.name: install_app_sim
tools.description: Installs an app in an iOS simulator. IMPORTANT: You MUST provide both the simulatorUuid and appPath parameters. Example: install_app_sim({ simulatorUuid: 'YOUR_UUID_HERE', appPath: '/path/to/your/app.app' })

simulatorUuid.description: UUID of the simulator to use (obtained from list_simulators)

appPath.description: Path to the .app bundle to install (full path to the .app directory)

tools.name: launch_app_logs_sim
tools.description: Launches an app in an iOS simulator and captures its logs.

simulatorUuid.description: UUID of the simulator to use (obtained from list_simulators)

bundleId.description: Bundle identifier of the app to launch (e.g., 'com.example.MyApp')

args.description: Additional arguments to pass to the app

tools.name: launch_app_sim
tools.description: Launches an app in an iOS simulator by UUID or name. If simulator window isn't visible, use open_sim() first. IMPORTANT: Provide either simulatorUuid OR simulatorName, plus bundleId. Note: You must install the app in the simulator before launching. The typical workflow is: build → install → launch. Example: launch_app_sim({ simulatorUuid: 'YOUR_UUID_HERE', bundleId: 'com.example.MyApp' }) or launch_app_sim({ simulatorName: 'iPhone 16', bundleId: 'com.example.MyApp' })

simulatorUuid.description: UUID of the simulator to use (obtained from list_simulators). Provide EITHER this OR simulatorName, not both

simulatorName.description: Name of the simulator (e.g., 'iPhone 16'). Provide EITHER this OR simulatorUuid, not both

bundleId.description: Bundle identifier of the app to launch (e.g., 'com.example.MyApp')

args.description: Additional arguments to pass to the app

tools.name: list_sims
tools.description: Lists available iOS simulators with their UUIDs.

enabled.description: Optional flag to enable the listing operation.

tools.name: open_sim
tools.description: Opens the iOS Simulator app.

tools.name: screenshot
tools.description: Captures screenshot for visual verification. For UI coordinates, use describe_ui instead (don't determine coordinates from screenshots).

simulatorUuid.description: UUID of the simulator (obtained from list_simulators). Provide EITHER this OR simulatorName, not both

simulatorName.description: Name of the simulator (e.g., 'iPhone 16'). Provide EITHER this OR simulatorUuid, not both

bundleId.description: Bundle identifier of the app to stop (e.g., 'com.example.MyApp')

tools.name: reset_sim_location
tools.description: Resets the simulator's location to default.

simulatorUuid.description: UUID of the simulator to use (obtained from list_simulators)

tools.name: set_sim_appearance
tools.description: Sets the appearance mode (dark/light) of an iOS simulator.

simulatorUuid.description: UUID of the simulator to use (obtained from list_simulators)

mode.description: The appearance mode to set (either "dark" or "light")

tools.name: set_sim_location
tools.description: Sets a custom GPS location for the simulator.

simulatorUuid.description: UUID of the simulator to use (obtained from list_simulators)

latitude.description: The latitude for the custom location.

longitude.description: The longitude for the custom location.

tools.name: sim_statusbar
tools.description: Sets the data network indicator in the iOS simulator status bar. Use "clear" to reset all overrides, or specify a network type (hide, wifi, 3g, 4g, lte, lte-a, lte+, 5g, 5g+, 5g-uwb, 5g-uc).

simulatorUuid.description: UUID of the simulator to use (obtained from list_simulators)

dataNetwork.description: Data network type to display in status bar. Use "clear" to reset all overrides. Valid values: clear, hide, wifi, 3g, 4g, lte, lte-a, lte+, 5g, 5g+, 5g-uwb, 5g-uc.

tools.name: swift_package_build
tools.description: Builds a Swift Package with swift build

packagePath.description: Path to the Swift package root (Required)

parseAsLibrary.description: Build as library instead of executable

tools.name: swift_package_clean
tools.description: Cleans Swift Package build artifacts and derived data

packagePath.description: Path to the Swift package root (Required)

tools.name: swift_package_list
tools.description: Lists currently running Swift Package processes

tools.name: swift_package_run
tools.description: Runs an executable target from a Swift Package with swift run

packagePath.description: Path to the Swift package root (Required)

executableName.description: Name of executable to run (defaults to package name)

arguments.description: Arguments to pass to the executable

background.description: Run in background and return immediately (default: false)

tools.name: swift_package_stop
tools.description: Stops a running Swift Package executable started with swift_package_run

pid.description: Process ID (PID) of the running executable

tools.name: swift_package_test
tools.description: Runs tests for a Swift Package with swift test

packagePath.description: Path to the Swift package root (Required)

testProduct.description: Optional specific test product to run

tools.name: button
tools.description: Press hardware button on iOS simulator. Supported buttons: apple-pay, home, lock, side-button, siri

tools.name: gesture
tools.description: Perform gesture on iOS simulator using preset gestures: scroll-up, scroll-down, scroll-left, scroll-right, swipe-from-left-edge, swipe-from-right-edge, swipe-from-top-edge, swipe-from-bottom-edge

preset.description: The gesture preset to perform. Must be one of: scroll-up, scroll-down, scroll-left, scroll-right, swipe-from-left-edge, swipe-from-right-edge, swipe-from-top-edge, swipe-from-bottom-edge.

screenWidth.description: Optional: Screen width in pixels. Used for gesture calculations. Auto-detected if not provided.

screenHeight.description: Optional: Screen height in pixels. Used for gesture calculations. Auto-detected if not provided.

duration.description: Optional: Duration of the gesture in seconds.

delta.description: Optional: Distance to move in pixels.

preDelay.description: Optional: Delay before starting the gesture in seconds.

postDelay.description: Optional: Delay after completing the gesture in seconds.

tools.name: key_press
tools.description: Press a single key by keycode on the simulator. Common keycodes: 40=Return, 42=Backspace, 43=Tab, 44=Space, 58-67=F1-F10.

tools.name: key_sequence
tools.description: Press key sequence using HID keycodes on iOS simulator with configurable delay

tools.name: long_press
tools.description: Long press at specific coordinates for given duration (ms). Use describe_ui for precise coordinates (don't guess from screenshots).

tools.name: swipe
tools.description: Swipe from one point to another. Use describe_ui for precise coordinates (don't guess from screenshots). Supports configurable timing.

tools.name: tap
tools.description: Tap at specific coordinates. Use describe_ui to get precise element coordinates (don't guess from screenshots). Supports optional timing delays.

tools.name: touch
tools.description: Perform touch down/up events at specific coordinates. Use describe_ui for precise coordinates (don't guess from screenshots).

tools.name: type_text
tools.description: Type text (supports US keyboard characters). Use describe_ui to find text field, tap to focus, then type.
